The previous vLLM core engine tracing (llm_request) is expensive. 🔴 With `--otlp-traces-endpoint` set, pooling requests' Prometheus latency metrics silently drop all tokenization and rendering time, so dashboards change when tracing is toggled. When `is_tracing_request` is true, `preprocessing()` overwrites each engine input's `prompts["arrival_time"]` with the time preprocessing finished. The engine uses that value as request arrival for e2e latency and TTFT. Fix: leave the renderer's `arrival_time` unchanged. Pass the preprocessing boundary to the span through the context or a span attribute instead, so turning tracing on does not change metric semantics.

<details>
<summary>Why this was flagged</summary>

Tracing is enabled with `--otlp-traces-endpoint`, so `observability_config.is_tracing_enabled` is true. A pooling request then goes through `PoolingBaseServing.preprocessing` (base/serving.py:97-104), which sets `engine_inputs["prompts"]["arrival_time"] = ctx.preprocessing_finished / TO_S`. Before that, the renderer had stamped `arrival_time = time.time()` at render start (renderers/base.py:1251, online_renderer.py:494-502). `InputProcessor` reads `prompt.get("arrival_time", ...)` at v1/engine/input_processor.py:404, and the engine uses it as the request arrival time for the stats and latency histograms. On the base branch, and with tracing off, arrival includes rendering and tokenization time. With tracing on, that time is excluded. As a result, the same server reports systematically lower e2e and TTFT latency just because an OTLP endpoint was configured. Nothing in the diff documents this side effect on metrics.

**Verification:** In `PoolingBaseServing.preprocessing` (vllm/entrypoints/pooling/base/serving.py), the new code runs `engine_inputs["prompts"]["arrival_time"] = ctx.preprocessing_finished / TO_S`. That overwrites the renderer's stamp (renderers/base.py:1251). So when tracing is on, the Prometheus e2e and TTFT metrics for pooling requests leave out rendering and tokenization time.

</details>

🔴 With tracing on, late-interaction scoring requests (ColBERT-style /score, /rerank) no longer pass the client's trace context to the engine. That trace context reached the engine before this change. Trace headers are now set on `ctx.trace_headers` only inside `maybe_tracing`/`engine_call`, and `flash_late_interaction` skips both. Its `query_ctx`/`doc_ctx` keep the default `trace_headers=None`. Fix: run `flash_late_interaction` inside `maybe_tracing` plus the engine_call span. Then copy `ctx.trace_headers` into `query_ctx` and `doc_ctx` so every `_prepare_generators` caller gets the headers.

<details>
<summary>Why this was flagged</summary>

`ServingScores.__call__` (scoring/serving.py:69-73) sends late-interaction models to `flash_late_interaction` when `enable_flash_late_interaction` is True, which is the default. That path calls `_init_ctx` and `_preprocessing_async` directly and never enters `maybe_tracing`, so `ctx.trace_headers` is never set. The new contexts at scoring/serving.py:256 and :298 do not copy it either. `_prepare_generators` (base/serving.py:232) now passes `trace_headers=ctx.trace_headers`, which is None, to `engine_client.encode`. On the base branch, `_prepare_generators` pulled the headers straight from `ctx.raw_request.headers`. After this change, operators with `--otlp-traces-endpoint` get llm_request spans for these requests that are cut off from the client trace, and the requests get no entrypoint spans.

**Verification:** The diff removes the `_get_trace_headers` call and passes `trace_headers=ctx.trace_headers` instead (base/serving.py:232). `flash_late_interaction` (scoring/serving.py lines 194-210) never enters `maybe_tracing` or `engine_call`. As a result, `engine_client.encode(..., trace_headers=None)` runs for every query and doc sub-request.

</details>

Those args are the router's `(request, raw_request)`, so `maybe_tracing` receives 5 positional arguments but accepts at most 4. Fix: pass only the raw request, e.g. resolve `raw_request` from args/kwargs and call `self.maybe_tracing(ctx, self.io_processor, raw_request)`, as `PoolingBaseServing.__call__` does.

<details>
<summary>Why this was flagged</summary>

The router calls `handler(request, raw_request)` (scoring/api_router.py:49,81). `ServingScores.__call__` (scoring/serving.py:75) passes those to `flash_late_interaction(*args, **kwargs)` whenever `enable_flash_late_interaction` is True, which is the default for late-interaction models. At scoring/serving.py:203 the new code runs `self.maybe_tracing(ctx, self.io_processor, *args, **kwargs)`, which expands to `maybe_tracing(ctx, io_processor, request, raw_request)`. Both `_ObservabilityMixin.maybe_tracing` and the OTel variant (base/observability.py) take `(self, ctx, io_processor, raw_request=None)`, so Python raises TypeError before any encoding runs, and the client gets a 500. On the base branch these requests succeed. The updated unit tests do not catch this: test_late_interaction_serving.py:88 calls `flash_late_interaction()` with no args, and test_late_interaction_online.py:55 raises during `_init_ctx` before reaching this line.

**Verification:** The new code at scoring/serving.py:203 runs `async with self.maybe_tracing(ctx, self.io_processor, *args, **kwargs):`, which becomes `maybe_tracing(ctx, io_processor, request, raw_request)`. Both versions of `maybe_tracing` take only `(self, ctx, io_processor, raw_request=None)`. Before this change, `flash_late_interaction` never called `maybe_tracing`, so these requests used to work.

</details>

🔴 With tracing on, late-interaction /score and /rerank spans, and any failed request, carry hugely negative latency values, e.g. `gen_ai.latency.preprocessing.ms` near -1.7e12. The `is not None` guards at observability.py:259-272 never fire, because `PoolingServeContext` defaults the timestamps to `0`, not `None`. `flash_late_interaction` never sets `preprocessing_finished`, so the code computes `(0 - arrival)`. Fix: emit each latency only when both of its timestamps were actually recorded. One way is to default the timestamp fields to `None`, or to check `> 0`. This covers the flash path and the paths that raise mid-request.

<details>
<summary>Why this was flagged</summary>

In typing.py, `PoolingServeContext` declares `arrival_time_ns`, `preprocessing_finished`, `engine_call_finished` and `postprocessing_finished` as `int = 0`. `_get_request_span_attributes` (observability.py:259-272) reads them with `getattr(..., None)` and guards with `is not None`, which is always true. `ServingScores.flash_late_interaction` (scoring/serving.py:196-215) sets `ctx.arrival_time_ns` and enters `maybe_tracing`, but it never calls `preprocessing`, `engine_call` or `postprocessing`, so the other three stay 0. Every traced late-interaction request therefore records `gen_ai.latency.preprocessing.ms = (0 - time_ns())/1e6`, roughly -1.7e12, plus 0 for the engine-call and postprocessing latencies. On the regular path, an exception in `_preprocessing_async` or the engine call leaves later timestamps at 0, and that likewise gives a negative or zero latency on the request span. These attributes are new, but operators who follow the PR's own 'Traces as Metrics' TraceQL query get corrupted aggregates.

**Verification:** normal. Trigger: tracing is enabled (`--otlp-traces-endpoint`) and the request is a late-interaction /score or /rerank (flash path, which is on by default) or any request that fails before postprocessing.

How it happens:
- typing.py adds `arrival_time_ns: int = 0`, `preprocessing_finished: int = 0`, `engine_call_finished: int = 0` and `postprocessing_finished: int = 0` to PoolingServeContext. None of them default to None.

</details>

🔴 Operators who name the service through `OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES=service.name=...` instead of `OTEL_SERVICE_NAME` will now see every vLLM trace under service "vllm". This includes the existing llm_request and worker traces. Their own name is ignored. `init_otel_trace_provider` always sets `service.name` in the explicit attributes passed to `Resource.create`, falling back to "vllm" when `OTEL_SERVICE_NAME` is unset. Explicit attributes override what the env detector reads. Fix: add `service.name` only when neither `OTEL_SERVICE_NAME` nor a `service.name` entry in `OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES` is set, e.g. by checking the detected resource first.

<details>
<summary>Why this was flagged</summary>

The trigger is a deployment that sets `OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES="service.name=my-embedder,..."` without `OTEL_SERVICE_NAME`, and then runs `vllm serve --otlp-traces-endpoint ...`. Every tracer goes through the new `init_otel_trace_provider` (vllm/tracing/otel.py:67). At otel.py:83-85 it builds `resource_attrs` with `SERVICE_NAME: os.environ.get("OTEL_SERVICE_NAME", "vllm")` and passes them to `Resource.create`. The OTel SDK merges the explicit attributes after its OTELResourceDetector output, which is parsed from `OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES`, so the explicit attributes win. As a result `service.name` becomes "vllm" for the API server, engine core and workers. On the base branch no `service.name` was passed explicitly, so the env-configured name was honored. After this change, traces land under a different service, and existing Tempo/Jaeger queries and dashboards keyed on the configured name silently go empty. Only `OTEL_SERVICE_NAME` is checked as a guard, and `OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES` is not.

**Verification:** In vllm/tracing/otel.py:82-88 the new code does `service_name = os.environ.get(OTEL_SERVICE_NAME, "vllm")` before calling `Resource.create(resource_attrs)`. The explicit attributes take precedence in that merge, so `service.name="vllm"` replaces the operator's value. On the base, `init_otel_tracer` passed only `vllm.instrumenting_module_name` and `vllm.process_id`, so a service.name set in OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES was kept.

</details>

🟡 (optional) With `--otlp-traces-endpoint` set, one API server process now builds several OTLP exporters and batch-processor threads. It also logs "Overriding of current TracerProvider is not allowed" at startup. Each pooling serving instance calls `_init_observability` (base/observability.py:56), and each call builds a new `TracerProvider`. Each one also calls `set_tracer_provider` and registers its own `atexit` shutdown. Fix: create the pooling trace provider once per process and reuse it across all `PoolingBaseServing` instances, for example with a module-level cached provider. Then `set_tracer_provider` runs only once. [also at: vllm/entrypoints/pooling/base/observability.py:57 - With tracing on, each pooling serving instance builds its own TracerProvider, OTLP exporter and batch thread. A pooling server makes up to three, and later ones log an override warning.]

<details>
<summary>Why this was flagged</summary>

`build_pooling_servings` (vllm/entrypoints/pooling/factories.py:172-217) creates `ServingPooling`, `ServingEmbedding` and/or `ServingClassification`, and `ServingScores` for a single model. With an embedding model that is three instances. Each runs `PoolingBaseServing.__init__`, which calls `_init_observability()`, which calls `init_otel_trace_provider` (otel.py:62-96). Each call creates a new `TracerProvider`, `get_span_exporter` connection and `BatchSpanProcessor` thread, calls the global `set_tracer_provider` and registers another `atexit` shutdown. OpenTelemetry ignores every `set_tracer_provider` call after the first and logs a warning each time. Before this change, pooling servings created no providers. After it, every API server process (times `api_server_count`) keeps N extra exporter connections and threads alive and prints override warnings at every startup.

**Verification:** The trigger is any API server started with `--otlp-traces-endpoint` and a pooling model. With tracing enabled, that calls `init_otel_trace_provider(...)` for every instance (base/observability.py:56). OTel only lets the global provider be set once, so each pooling call to `set_tracer_provider` logs the "Overriding of current TracerProvider is not allowed" warning.

</details>

🟡 (optional) With tracing on, a pooling request cancelled by client disconnect gets no "cancelled" marker on its spans. OTel also logs a warning for each span closed by the cancellation. `Status(StatusCode.UNSET, "cancelled")` is rejected by the OTel API: it logs "description should only be set when status_code is set to StatusCode.ERROR" and drops the description. Fix: record cancellation in a way OTel keeps on both the request span and the child-span helper, e.g. `span.set_attribute("vllm.request.cancelled", True)` or `span.add_event("cancelled")`, with no status description.

<details>
<summary>Why this was flagged</summary>

Pooling routes are wrapped in `@ with_cancellation` (embed/api_router.py:36, scoring/api_router.py:45, classify/api_router.py:27, pooling/api_router.py:35), so a client disconnect raises CancelledError inside `maybe_tracing`, and inside `maybe_start_span_async` for the active stage. Both handlers build `Status(StatusCode.UNSET, "cancelled")` (observability.py:169 and :233). The opentelemetry-api `Status.__init__` logs the warning above and leaves the description as None when the code is not ERROR. So the spans end up UNSET with no cancellation information, which means the feature the PR describes ("mark cancellations as UNSET" with a "cancelled" reason) records nothing. Each disconnected request also adds two warning lines, which can flood logs under heavy disconnect churn. The base branch had no pooling spans, so neither the spam nor the lost marker existed. No test in test_observability.py exercises the cancellation path.

**Verification:** Trigger: tracing is enabled and a client disconnects from a pooling route. On disconnect, CancelledError reaches two handlers in vllm/entrypoints/pooling/base/observability.py: line 169 and line 233. In opentelemetry-api, `Status.__init__` only keeps a description when the code is ERROR. A cancelled request's spans just end as UNSET with no marker.

</details>

When `is_tracing_request` is true, `preprocessing()` overwrites each engine input's `prompts["arrival_time"]` with the time preprocessing finished. The `is not None` guards at observability.py:259-272 never fire, because `PoolingServeContext` defaults the timestamps to `0`, not `None`. `flash_late_interaction` never sets `preprocessing_finished`, so the code computes `(0 - arrival)`. <summary>Why this was flagged</summary>

This includes the existing llm_request and worker traces. Their own name is ignored. `init_otel_trace_provider` always sets `service.name` in the explicit attributes passed to `Resource.create`, falling back to "vllm" when `OTEL_SERVICE_NAME` is unset. Explicit attributes override what the env detector reads. Fix: add `service.name` only when neither `OTEL_SERVICE_NAME` nor a `service.name` entry in `OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES` is set, e.g. by checking the detected resource first.

<details>
<summary>Why this was flagged</summary>

The trigger is a deployment that sets `OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES="service.name=my-embedder,..."` without `OTEL_SERVICE_NAME`, and then runs `vllm serve --otlp-traces-endpoint ...`. Every tracer goes through the new `init_otel_trace_provider` (vllm/tracing/otel.py:67). At otel.py:83-85 it builds `resource_attrs` with `SERVICE_NAME: os.environ.get("OTEL_SERVICE_NAME", "vllm")` and passes them to `Resource.create`. The OTel SDK merges the explicit attributes after its OTELResourceDetector output, which is parsed from `OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES`, so the explicit attributes win. **Verification:** In vllm/tracing/otel.py:82-88 the new code does `service_name = os.environ.get(OTEL_SERVICE_NAME, "vllm")` before calling `Resource.create(resource_attrs)`. On the base, `init_otel_tracer` passed only `vllm.instrumenting_module_name` and `vllm.process_id`, so a service.name set in OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES was kept.

It also logs "Overriding of current TracerProvider is not allowed" at startup. Each pooling serving instance calls `_init_observability` (base/observability.py:56), and each call builds a new `TracerProvider`. Each one also calls `set_tracer_provider` and registers its own `atexit` shutdown. Then `set_tracer_provider` runs only once. [also at: vllm/entrypoints/pooling/base/observability.py:57 - With tracing on, each pooling serving instance builds its own TracerProvider, OTLP exporter and batch thread. A pooling server makes up to three, and later ones log an override warning.]

<details>
<summary>Why this was flagged</summary>

`build_pooling_servings` (vllm/entrypoints/pooling/factories.py:172-217) creates `ServingPooling`, `ServingEmbedding` and/or `ServingClassification`, and `ServingScores` for a single model. With an embedding model that is three instances. Each runs `PoolingBaseServing.__init__`, which calls `_init_observability()`, which calls `init_otel_trace_provider` (otel.py:62-96). Each call creates a new `TracerProvider`, `get_span_exporter` connection and `BatchSpanProcessor` thread, calls the global `set_tracer_provider` and registers another `atexit` shutdown. OpenTelemetry ignores every `set_tracer_provider` call after the first and logs a warning each time. Before this change, pooling servings created no providers. After it, every API server process (times `api_server_count`) keeps N extra exporter connections and threads alive and prints override warnings at every startup.

**Verification:** The trigger is any API server started with `--otlp-traces-endpoint` and a pooling model. With tracing enabled, that calls `init_otel_trace_provider(...)` for every instance (base/observability.py:56). OTel only lets the global provider be set once, so each pooling call to `set_tracer_provider` logs the "Overriding of current TracerProvider is not allowed" warning.

</details>

🟡 (optional) With tracing on, a pooling request cancelled by client disconnect gets no "cancelled" marker on its spans. OTel also logs a warning for each span closed by the cancellation. `Status(StatusCode.UNSET, "cancelled")` is rejected by the OTel API: it logs "description should only be set when status_code is set to StatusCode.ERROR" and drops the description. Fix: record cancellation in a way OTel keeps on both the request span and the child-span helper, e.g. `span.set_attribute("vllm.request.cancelled", True)` or `span.add_event("cancelled")`, with no status description.

<details>
<summary>Why this was flagged</summary>

Pooling routes are wrapped in `@ with_cancellation` (embed/api_router.py:36, scoring/api_router.py:45, classify/api_router.py:27, pooling/api_router.py:35), so a client disconnect raises CancelledError inside `maybe_tracing`, and inside `maybe_start_span_async` for the active stage. Both handlers build `Status(StatusCode.UNSET, "cancelled")` (observability.py:169 and :233). The opentelemetry-api `Status.__init__` logs the warning above and leaves the description as None when the code is not ERROR. So the spans end up UNSET with no cancellation information, which means the feature the PR describes ("mark cancellations as UNSET" with a "cancelled" reason) records nothing. Each disconnected request also adds two warning lines, which can flood logs under heavy disconnect churn. The base branch had no pooling spans, so neither the spam nor the lost marker existed. No test in test_observability.py exercises the cancellation path.

**Verification:** Trigger: tracing is enabled and a client disconnects from a pooling route. On disconnect, CancelledError reaches two handlers in vllm/entrypoints/pooling/base/observability.py: line 169 and line 233. In opentelemetry-api, `Status.__init__` only keeps a description when the code is ERROR. A cancelled request's spans just end as UNSET with no marker.

</details>
